transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My mind keeps swinging between being full of plans and then feeling so foggy that I can’t focus long enough to finish anything. It has been really frustrating to deal with, especially since I'm trying to build up my freelance work right now.
Can you tell me more about these swings in your mind, specifically how your mood changes and if you've noticed any patterns or triggers for these shifts?

I'll swing from feeling incredibly upbeat and convinced everything is amazing, to snapping at my husband over tiny things like how he loads the dishwasher. These disruptive shifts really started about four months ago when I left my structured job to focus on my art therapy certificate, which left my daily routine a lot looser.

Have you experienced any periods of abnormally elevated mood or irritability that lasted for several days or more, where you felt little need for sleep, were more talkative than usual, or engaged in impulsive behaviors?

Yes, during these high phases over the last four months, I stay up very late working on projects and talk in a nonstop stream that my husband can't even interrupt. I'll impulsively take on massive tasks, like emailing a dozen organizations or redesigning my whole website in a single night. I also get so irritable that I snap at my husband over the tiniest things.

Have you experienced any periods of feeling persistently sad, empty, or hopeless that lasted for several days or more, where you lost interest in activities you once enjoyed, had changes in appetite or sleep, or had difficulty concentrating?

Yes, for about the last three months I've been stuck in this low, foggy phase where I've lost all interest in things I used to love, like my book club and sketching. My appetite has been totally off—some days I just pick at crackers and my clothes are fitting looser—and the brain fog is so bad that I end up rereading the same paragraph over and over without any of it sinking in.
Can you estimate how often these high and low phases occur, and do they tend to follow each other in a pattern, or do they seem to happen randomly?

They don't feel random; it started about four months ago when I transitioned to freelance with an intense, high-energy planning phase. That initial rush lasted for a bit, but then it turned into a steep crash, and I've been stuck in this low, foggy phase for most of the last three months. It really felt like the high phase directly triggered this long, heavy low.
Can you describe the typical duration of your high-energy phases before they transition into the low, foggy phases, and have you noticed any consistent pattern to how long each phase lasts?

Those high-energy, revved-up phases usually last for a few weeks at a time, where I feel incredibly active and charged up. In contrast, the low, foggy periods are much more prolonged, and this current low phase has been dragging on for roughly the last three months.
Do your high-energy phases typically last less than four days, or do they often last longer, transitioning into more prolonged periods of elevated mood or irritability?

They definitely last longer than just four days, usually stretching on for weeks at a time where I feel highly active and irritable. It has been a consistent part of the overall four-month pattern of ups and downs I've been dealing with.

Can you confirm whether these high-energy phases have ever lasted less than four days, or if they consistently last longer, often transitioning into more prolonged periods of elevated mood or irritability?

They consistently last much longer than four days, usually stretching on for weeks at a time. During those weeks, I feel a sustained high mood, lots of irritability, and a constant rush of ideas before it eventually gives way to the long, foggy low periods.
Have you experienced any episodes of depression that lasted for at least two weeks, which is a key distinction between some mood disorders?

Yes, definitely. This current low, foggy period has been hanging around most days for roughly the last three months, which is way longer than two weeks. It has made it incredibly hard for me to function or get anything done.
Can you clarify if your high-energy phases and low, foggy phases have occurred in a regular, cyclic pattern over the past four months, or if they seem to be more sporadic and unpredictable?

They actually feel highly disruptive and unpredictable. Since leaving my job four months ago, I had that initial high-energy phase of intense planning, which was followed by a steep, prolonged drop. This low, foggy stretch has been hanging around most days for roughly the last three months, making my energy and productivity very hard to predict.
Have you experienced any full episodes of mania or hypomania, where your high-energy periods were not followed by such a prolonged low, foggy phase, or do the highs always seem to precede these lows?

I'm not entirely sure about past patterns or isolated episodes, as I've mostly just been focused on this current cycle over the last four months. During this time, my high-energy planning phases have felt directly followed by a steep, foggy crash, and I don't recall having high periods before this that didn't eventually lead into a low phase.

Can you think of any time in the past when you had a high-energy phase that did not eventually lead to one of these prolonged low, foggy periods, or have all your high-energy phases been followed by a crash like the ones you've described over the last four months?

This pattern of swinging between intense highs and crashing into foggy lows is actually quite new to me. It only started about four months ago after I left my steady job to focus on freelance work. I don't recall ever having these kinds of disruptive high-energy phases or subsequent crashes before this recent period.
Have you ever experienced a period of elevated mood or increased energy that lasted for at least four consecutive days but less than seven days, without being followed by a significant low phase?

No, I haven't experienced those high phases on their own without a crash. For me, any period of high energy always leads directly into a steep drop and a prolonged low phase. That foggy, low phase is what I've been stuck in for about three months now.

Can you confirm if there was ever a time when you experienced a distinct period of elevated mood or irritability lasting at least four consecutive days but less than two weeks, which was not immediately followed by a significant depressive episode, helping to clarify the nature of your mood swings?

I'm not quite sure about the exact number of days or the specific sequence of those periods. It is just really hard to keep track of the exact timeline when my mind is constantly swinging back and forth like this.

Can you try to recall if there was ever a high-energy phase that lasted for a few weeks without being immediately followed by a low, foggy phase, or have all your high phases directly led into these prolonged lows?

When this all started about four months ago, I had a highly energetic, exhilarating phase that lasted for about a month. That initial high was indeed followed by a steep, prolonged drop into this foggy, low state that has lasted for the past three months. Now, even when I get brief, revved-up spikes of energy, they quickly dump me right back into the heavy fog.

Can you recall any instance where you had a high-energy phase that was not followed by a low phase, or have you always transitioned from a high to a low, which could help differentiate between bipolar II disorder and major depressive disorder with manic episodes?

Since these mood swings started about four months ago, my initial high-energy phase of intense planning and website building was indeed followed by a steep, prolonged drop into this foggy, low state. It has felt like a continuous cycle of swinging back and forth between these two extremes, rather than having a high phase that just faded back to a normal baseline without a crash.

Can you remember any specific instance in the past four months where you experienced a distinct period of elevated mood or irritability that lasted at least four consecutive days but less than two weeks, and this period was not immediately followed by a significant depressive episode?

I'm not really sure about the exact number of days or if there was ever a high period that didn't end in a crash. It feels like my mood is constantly swinging, and those highly productive phases usually lead right into the foggy, low periods. Because of that, it's really hard for me to track the exact duration of each phase.

Can you recall any instance where you had a period of elevated mood or irritability that lasted at least four consecutive days but less than two weeks, without being followed by a significant low phase, which could help clarify if you've experienced hypomanic episodes?
I'm not quite sure. As far as I can remember, my high, revved-up phases have almost always been followed by those deep, foggy crashes, rather than happening on their own without a low phase.

Can you think of any time in the past four months when you had a period of elevated mood or increased energy that was not part of a cycle leading to a low, foggy phase, but rather stood alone as a distinct episode?

No, none of my high-energy periods have stood alone over the last four months. They have always felt connected to the cycle, typically being followed by a steep drop into that low, foggy phase. It really feels like a continuous, disruptive roller coaster of swinging back and forth rather than isolated, independent episodes.

Have you ever had a period where you felt abnormally happy, energetic, or irritable for several days, but it didn't significantly interfere with your daily life or relationships, and wasn't followed by a depressive episode?

No, those high periods definitely cause a lot of problems for me and my relationships, like arguing with my husband and missing important work deadlines. They also aren't harmless or isolated, because they almost always end in a deep, foggy crash. I've never had a high phase that didn't disrupt my life or lead straight into a low period.

Can you recall any instance where you experienced a distinct period of elevated mood or irritability that lasted at least four consecutive days but less than two weeks, without significant impairment in social or occupational functioning, which could indicate a hypomanic episode?

I can't recall a period of high energy or elevated mood that didn't eventually cause some kind of disruption or trouble. My high phases usually last for weeks and tend to lead to unfinished projects and a lot of strain on my relationships.

Can you recall any instance where you had a period of elevated mood or irritability that lasted at least four consecutive days, where you didn't experience significant impairment in your daily life or relationships, and this period wasn't followed by a depressive episode?

No, I really can't recall a high phase that didn't cause problems or wasn't followed by a crash. Whenever I get into those highly active states, it always ends up disrupting my life—like causing arguments with my husband or making me miss deadlines—and then I inevitably drop into a long, foggy low period.

Can you describe any period of elevated mood or increased energy where you felt unusually happy or irritable for at least four consecutive days, but it didn't significantly interfere with your daily life or relationships, and wasn't followed by a noticeable low phase?

No, I have never experienced a high phase like that. Whenever I have those periods of elevated mood or high energy, they always end up causing significant problems, like missing deadlines, letting down my community group, and arguing with my husband. On top of that, they are always followed by a steep, prolonged low phase where I feel completely drained.

Can you think of any time when you had a high-energy phase that didn't significantly impair your daily functioning or relationships and also wasn't followed by a low phase, which might help distinguish between different types of mood disorders?

I really can't recall any high-energy periods that didn't cause issues or weren't followed by a low phase. My experience has mostly just been the disruptive cycle of swinging back and forth that I've described over the last few months.

Can you recall any instance where you had a period of elevated mood or irritability that lasted at least four consecutive days, where you didn't experience significant impairment in your daily life or relationships, and this period was characterized by at least three of the following: inflated self-esteem, decreased need for sleep, more talkative than usual, flight of ideas, distractibility, increase in goal-directed activity, or excessive involvement in pleasurable activities that have a high potential for painful consequences, without being followed by a depressive episode?

No, those high periods where my thoughts race, I talk nonstop, and I make massive plans never happen without causing major problems. They always cause serious disruptions, like strained relationships and missed deadlines, and they always end in a steep crash into that foggy, low phase. I've never had a high phase that was harmless or stood on its own.

Can you recall any specific instance where you experienced a distinct period of elevated mood or irritability that lasted at least four consecutive days but less than two weeks, with at least three symptoms such as inflated self-esteem, decreased need for sleep, or excessive involvement in pleasurable activities, and this period was not immediately followed by a significant depressive episode?

I'm not really sure about the exact number of days or the specific sequence you're asking about. My high and low phases have tended to blur together over the last few months, and I haven't tracked them closely enough to know if a high period lasted exactly that long without being followed by a low period.

Can you recall any instance where you had a period of elevated mood or irritability that lasted at least four consecutive days, but less than two weeks, with symptoms such as inflated self-esteem, decreased need for sleep, or excessive involvement in pleasurable activities, and this period was not immediately followed by a significant depressive episode, and did not cause significant impairment in your daily life or relationships?

I don't recall ever having a high period that didn't cause problems or wasn't followed by a crash. For me, those high phases usually lead to arguments with my husband and unfinished projects, and they are almost always followed by a long, foggy low period.

Can you think of any instance where you had a distinct period of elevated mood or irritability lasting at least four consecutive days but less than two weeks, with symptoms like decreased need for sleep or excessive involvement in activities, that didn't significantly impair your daily life or relationships and wasn't followed by a depressive episode?

I can't really think of a time like that. Whenever I've had those high-energy or intense planning phases, they have almost always ended up causing problems with my work or relationships, and they are usually followed by a heavy crash or a long period of feeling low and foggy.

Have you ever experienced a period of elevated mood or irritability that met the criteria for a hypomanic episode, such as lasting at least four consecutive days, but did not cause significant impairment in your daily life or relationships and was not followed by a major depressive episode?

No, my high periods have definitely not been harmless. They have caused real disruptions in my life, like missing important deadlines and straining my relationship with my husband, and they have always been followed by those long, foggy, low periods over the last few months.

Can you recall any instance where you had a period of elevated mood or irritability that lasted at least four consecutive days, with symptoms such as inflated self-esteem, decreased need for sleep, or excessive involvement in pleasurable activities, and this period was not immediately followed by a significant depressive episode and did not cause significant impairment in your social or occupational functioning?

No, my high periods don't match that description at all. They have always been followed by a steep, prolonged crash, and they absolutely caused significant disruptions like missing major grant deadlines and straining my marriage.
